meta.title: EDA → MLP Excellent Path: Business & Technical Decision Graph
meta.description: Knowledge graph showing optimal decision paths (excellent scoring) vs alternative paths (qualified scoring) through phishing detection ML pipeline

nodes.label: Phishing Detection Problem
nodes.description: $90M fraud exposure: 45% of attacks missed at baseline

nodes.label: Business-First Framing
nodes.description: Lead with fraud exposure ($90M), customer impact (credential theft), and hard KPIs (Recall≥70%, FPR≤5%)
nodes.reasoning: Stakeholder-centric: translates technical ML problem into business value proposition. Establishes clear success criteria upfront.

nodes.label: Technical-First Framing
nodes.description: Define as binary classification with 15 features, class imbalance 55:45
nodes.reasoning: ML-centric: accurate but misses business context. Stakeholders hear jargon without understanding 'why this matters'.

nodes.label: EDA Profiling
nodes.description: Dataset: 11,430 websites × 15 features

nodes.label: Evidence-Based EDA
nodes.description: Create EDA findings → Pipeline decisions traceability table. Every insight documented with business impact.
nodes.reasoning: Scientific rigor: each data quality issue mapped to (1) business impact, (2) preprocessing solution, (3) model improvement. Audit-ready.
nodes.business_impact: Enables regulatory explainability: 'Why did you log-transform?' → 'EDA showed skewness=5.2 → gradient instability → 500 epochs vs 120.'
nodes.technical_depth: Systematic profiling: missingness patterns (MNAR detection), distribution analysis (skewness thresholds), correlation analysis (multicollinearity)

nodes.label: Standard EDA
nodes.description: Run df.describe(), check missing values, plot histograms. Document in notebook cells.
nodes.reasoning: Mechanically correct but lacks narrative. Findings exist but not synthesized into actionable insights or business framing.
nodes.technical_depth: Basic profiling: summary statistics, null counts, basic plots. Missing: why these findings matter for model performance.

nodes.label: Class Imbalance 55:45
nodes.description: Legitimate 55.04%, Phishing 44.96%
nodes.business_impact: Without stratification: model bias → 44.96% attacks missed → $90M exposure

nodes.label: Impossible Values
nodes.description: 377 rows: NoOfImage < 0 (impossible)
nodes.business_impact: Corrupted data → model learns invalid patterns → production failures on valid inputs

nodes.label: Heavy Skewness
nodes.description: 10 features |skew|>1 (NoOfPopup: skew=8.1)
nodes.business_impact: Gradient instability → 500+ epochs convergence → training cost $X, slower iteration cycles

nodes.label: Top Predictor: DomainAge
nodes.description: r=0.333 correlation with target (highest)
nodes.business_impact: Key fraud signal: younger domains = higher phishing risk (adversaries use new domains to evade blocklists)

nodes.label: Stratified 70/15/15 Split
nodes.description: Preserve 55:45 class balance across train/val/test
nodes.reasoning: Evidence-linked: Class imbalance finding → Stratified split solution. Prevents distribution shift between sets.
nodes.alternative: Random split (qualified approach): Risks train 50:50 but test 60:40 → misleading metrics.
nodes.business_impact: Valid model evaluation: metrics on test set representative of production. Prevents false confidence.

nodes.label: Random 70/15/15 Split
nodes.description: Standard random split without stratification
nodes.reasoning: Standard practice but ignores class imbalance. May work if lucky but no guarantee of balanced splits.
nodes.risk: Test set could have 60:40 split → model optimized for 55:45 performs differently → invalid evaluation.

nodes.label: Clip NoOfImage<0 to 0
nodes.description: Fix impossible values before training
nodes.reasoning: Evidence-linked: Impossible values finding → Clip transformation. Prevents model from learning 'negative images predict legitimate'.
nodes.business_impact: Production robustness: model won't fail on valid data (images always ≥0 in real websites).

nodes.label: Drop Rows with NoOfImage<0
nodes.description: Remove 377 corrupted rows
nodes.reasoning: Removes bad data but loses 3.3% of training samples. Simple solution but suboptimal.
nodes.risk: Reduced training set → slightly worse model performance. Also doesn't address 'why' data was corrupted.

nodes.label: Log-Transform Skewed Features
nodes.description: Apply log(x+1) to 10 features with |skew|>1
nodes.reasoning: Evidence-linked with mathematical justification: Skewness → Gradient instability. Log compresses [0,1000] to [0,6.9] → stable gradients → 120 epochs vs 500+.
nodes.business_impact: Training efficiency: 4× faster convergence → reduced compute costs, faster iteration cycles for feature engineering.
nodes.technical_depth: Gradient formula: ∇L = (1/m)X^T(σ(Xθ) - y). Extreme X values → exploding gradients → tiny learning rate → slow convergence.

nodes.label: No Transformation (Scale Only)
nodes.description: Apply StandardScaler without addressing skewness
nodes.reasoning: Scaling helps but doesn't fix heavy tails. Gradient descent still unstable. Convergence slow.
nodes.consequence: 500+ epochs needed, or model doesn't converge fully → suboptimal coefficients.

nodes.label: Create Missing-Value Flags
nodes.description: Binary indicators for DomainAge_missing, Robots_missing, IsResponsive_missing
nodes.reasoning: MNAR pattern detection: Phishing sites deliberately omit metadata. Missing-value flags capture this fraud signal rather than losing it via imputation.
nodes.business_impact: Additional predictive feature: 'DomainAge_missing=1' itself predicts phishing. Improves recall by 2-3%.
nodes.technical_depth: Understands MCAR vs MAR vs MNAR. Creates indicator before imputation to preserve information.

nodes.label: Median Imputation Only
nodes.description: Fill missing values with median (numeric) or mode (categorical)
nodes.reasoning: Standard practice but loses MNAR information. Treats missingness as nuisance rather than signal.
nodes.missed_opportunity: Phishing sites hide metadata deliberately. This pattern is predictive but gets erased by imputation.

nodes.label: Train Logistic Regression (Baseline)
nodes.description: NumPy gradient descent: lr=0.1, epochs=120, L2=0.001
nodes.reasoning: Both candidates train baseline. Excellent candidate derives gradient descent from scratch and documents mathematical justification. Qualified candidate uses sklearn.
nodes.business_impact: Fast inference (1ms), explainable (coefficients), but insufficient discrimination for KPIs.

nodes.label: Train XGBoost (Performance)
nodes.description: Gradient boosting: max_depth=6, lr=0.2, n_estimators=80
nodes.reasoning: Justified with trade-off analysis: 0.06 AUC gain over Logistic = 600 fewer missed attacks per 10K samples = $1.2M annual value. Worth 10× latency cost for fraud detection.
nodes.business_impact: Best discrimination but violates FPR constraint. Explainability requires SHAP.
nodes.technical_depth: Captures feature interactions: 'DomainAge<6mo AND NoOfExternalRef>50 AND Industry=Unknown → high risk' that Logistic misses.

nodes.label: Train Neural Network
nodes.description: Deep learning with 3 hidden layers
nodes.reasoning: Inappropriate for tabular data with 11,430 samples. NNs need 100K+ for tabular. Trees dominate this domain.
nodes.consequence: Longer training time (30+ min vs 2 min for XGBoost), likely worse performance due to insufficient data.

nodes.label: Threshold Tuning on Validation Set
nodes.description: Sweep 1000 thresholds [0.0, 1.0], maximize recall subject to FPR≤5%
nodes.reasoning: Constrained optimization: Finds optimal threshold (0.65 for XGBoost) that balances recall-FPR trade-off. Uses validation set to prevent test set overfitting.
nodes.result: Tuned: Recall 75.2%, FPR 4.8% (meets FPR constraint, marginal on recall)
nodes.business_impact: Quantifies KPI gap: Even optimal threshold can't hit recall≥70% AND FPR≤5% simultaneously → needs better features.
nodes.technical_depth: Understands this is Pareto frontier problem. Threshold tuning moves along curve; feature engineering shifts curve.

nodes.label: Use Default Threshold 0.5
nodes.description: Standard binary classification threshold
nodes.reasoning: Simple but arbitrary. Doesn't optimize for business constraints (FPR≤5%). Misses opportunity to balance precision-recall.
nodes.consequence: XGBoost at 0.5: Recall 86.5% (good) but FPR 18.2% (violates constraint by 3.6×). Model appears strong on paper but unusable in production.

nodes.label: Critical Gap: KPIs Not Met
nodes.description: No model achieves recall≥70% AND FPR≤5% simultaneously
nodes.business_impact: Feature coverage insufficient. Current features (metadata only) max out at 0.888 AUC. Need text features to shift Pareto frontier.
nodes.reasoning: Proactive acknowledgment: Gap identified, root cause analyzed (feature limitations), iteration plan proposed (text features, SSL certs, 6-week timeline).

nodes.label: Gap Not Acknowledged
nodes.description: Reports XGBoost 0.888 AUC as success without discussing FPR violation
nodes.reasoning: Focuses on positive metric (AUC) while ignoring constraint violation (FPR 18.2% >> 5%). Lacks self-awareness or hides problem.
nodes.risk: Stakeholders discover gap later → credibility damaged. Model deployed as-is → 18% false alarm rate → customer complaints.

nodes.label: 6-Week Feature Engineering Sprint
nodes.description: Week 1-2: Text features (TFIDF, embeddings). Week 3-4: SSL + behavioral. Week 5-6: Retrain + A/B test.
nodes.reasoning: Concrete action plan with timeline: (1) Identifies high-impact features (text = +5-10% F1 per literature), (2) Phases work (quick wins → complex features), (3) Validates via A/B test.
nodes.business_impact: Expected outcome: 85% recall at 3% FPR after text features. Interim: Deploy warning mode (no hard block) to collect labels while building v2.

nodes.label: Deploy Current Model
nodes.description: Ship XGBoost with 0.888 AUC to production
nodes.reasoning: Ignores FPR constraint. Assumes 'high AUC = good model' without business context. Leads to production incident (18% false alarm rate).
nodes.consequence: Customer support flooded with complaints about blocked legitimate sites. Product team loses trust in ML team.

nodes.label: Hybrid Deployment Architecture
nodes.description: Logistic for 90% easy cases (1ms) + XGBoost for 10% borderline (10ms) → 1.9ms avg latency, 0.87 AUC
nodes.reasoning: Creative problem-solving: Balances latency constraint (<100ms) with performance. Logistic handles high-confidence cases fast; XGBoost refines borderline.
nodes.business_impact: Meets latency requirement (1.9ms << 100ms), 95% of XGBoost performance (0.87 vs 0.888 AUC), explainable for most cases (Logistic coefficients).
nodes.technical_depth: Understands ensemble architectures. Cascade classifier: fast model filters → complex model refines.

nodes.label: Split Validation
nodes.description: Class distribution logged: Train 55.1:44.9, Val 54.8:45.2, Test 55.0:45.0

nodes.label: Data Quality Check
nodes.description: Post-preprocessing: 0 rows with NoOfImage<0, all features ≥0

nodes.label: Convergence Speed
nodes.description: Logistic with log-transform: 120 epochs. Without: 500+ epochs (4× slower)
nodes.evidence: Loss curve shows plateau at epoch 120 (with transform) vs 500+ (without)

nodes.label: Model Performance Matrix
nodes.description: Logistic: 0.825 AUC, 81% recall, 22% FPR. KNN: 0.809 AUC, 82% recall, 29% FPR. XGBoost: 0.888 AUC, 87% recall, 18% FPR.
nodes.business_interpretation: XGBoost best but all violate FPR≤5%. Even after tuning, max recall at FPR≤5% is 75% (marginal).

excellent_narrative.label: Excellent Candidate Path
excellent_narrative.business_impact: $12.75M net ROI (current baseline) → $15.65M after 6-week iteration (+$2.9M value from feature engineering)
excellent_narrative.technical_depth: Graduate-level: Gradient descent derivation, Bayesian L2 interpretation, MNAR detection, constrained optimization
excellent_narrative.communication: Exceptional: Translates technical → business, uses analogies (security guard, suspicion meter), stakeholder-friendly

qualified_narrative.label: Qualified Candidate Path
key_gaps: KPI gap not acknowledged (or discovered late)
qualified_narrative.business_impact: Model trained but not deployable (FPR 18.2% >> 5%). Stakeholders discover gap later → credibility damaged.
qualified_narrative.technical_depth: Adequate: Correct implementations but surface-level understanding. Can't explain 'why' decisions matter.
qualified_narrative.communication: Functional: Can present findings but doesn't translate to stakeholder language.

poor_narrative.label: Poor Candidate Path (Anti-Pattern)
critical_failures: Inappropriate model choice (Neural Net for 11,430 tabular samples)
poor_narrative.business_impact: Production incident: 18% false alarm rate → customer complaints → model rolled back → ML team loses credibility.
poor_narrative.technical_depth: Insufficient: Fundamental misunderstanding of when to use NNs vs trees.
poor_narrative.communication: Poor: Cannot explain decisions to stakeholders.

characteristics: Proactive gap acknowledgment with iteration plans
Decisions lack deep justification ('it's common practice')
Inappropriate model choices (NN for small tabular data)

query_examples.query: What decisions differentiate excellent from qualified candidates?
query_examples.cypher: MATCH path = (e:decision {scoring:'excellent'})-[:excellent_path*]->(i:insight) WHERE e.selected = true RETURN path
query_examples.insight: Excellent path: Business framing → Evidence-based EDA → Mathematical justification for transforms → Threshold tuning → Gap acknowledgment → Iteration plan. Qualified path: Technical framing → Standard EDA → No math justification → Default threshold → Gap missed.

query_examples.query: Show evidence chain from EDA finding to business outcome
query_examples.cypher: MATCH path = (f:insight {layer:2})-[:informs]->(d:decision)-[:produces|validates|enables*]->(r:result|insight) WHERE d.selected = true RETURN path
query_examples.insight: Example: 'Class imbalance (55:45)' → 'Stratified split' → 'Validation: balanced splits' → 'Model comparison' → 'KPI gap discovery' → '$2.9M iteration value quantified'

query_examples.query: What business impact does log-transform have?
query_examples.insight: Training efficiency: 4× faster convergence (120 vs 500+ epochs) → reduced compute costs, faster iteration cycles for feature engineering → enables 6-week sprint vs 24-week.
